code.note: Single Fortran file: subroutine CUBTRI with its helpers (RNDERR, CUBRUL) and the test driver KONYN, which runs seven integrands at EPS = 1e-3 down to 1e-9 and prints the actual error against ACTUAL(k).

claim.location: Test driver KONYN in 584.gz (driver section, extracted line 36 (sequence column MAN 330); the comment above it is MAN 300-320): ACTUAL(4) = .6918104506612316, the integral of EXP(SIN(X)*COS(Y)) over 0<=X<=1, 0<=Y<=1-X (the comment credits it to Haegemans 1977). For IDATA=4 the driver sets T to vertices (0,1), (0,0), (1,0), and it calls CUBTRI with EPS=1E-3 first.

reference.sha256: see archive sha256 above; rerun should read the archive member

claim.metric: ANS returned by CUBTRI for integrand 4 (EXP(SIN(X)*COS(Y))) over the triangle with vertices (0,1), (0,0), (1,0), at EPS=1E-3, MCALLS=20000, NW=5000, with IER=0 expected.
claim.paper_value: 0.6918104506612316 from the shipped driver's ACTUAL(4). The ACM article is not read here; this value is the driver's reference, not a number taken from the paper text.

values.name: integral of EXP(SIN(X)*COS(Y)) over the driver's triangle

tolerance.basis: The routine's accuracy contract is a relative error of the requested EPS (the driver's first row is EPS=1E-3). Applied to the reference, that is an absolute tolerance of 1e-3 times 0.69181045 = 6.918e-4. Set before any run and not to be loosened after a run. The driver's own actual-error column reads |ANS - ACTUAL(4)|; a failure at this EPS means CUBTRI missed its own contract.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute (one CUBTRI call at EPS=1E-3 with MCALLS=20000).
cost.data_size: None; the integrand and triangle are in the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS archive.

why: The integral of EXP(SIN(X)*COS(Y)) has no closed form, so CUBTRI has to run to reproduce the 16-digit reference the driver checks against; the other ACTUAL values are closed forms and are not used.
